court: The European Court of Human Rights (Second Section)

facts.text: The case originated in an application (no. 34503/97) against the Republic of Turkey lodged with the European Commission of Human Rights by two Turkish nationals, Mr Kemal Demir and Ms Vicdan Baykara, on 8 October 1996.

anchor.surface_text: 1.  The case originated in an application (no. 34503/97) against the Republic of Turkey lodged with the European Commission of Human Rights (“the Commission”) under former Article 25 of the Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms (“the Convention”) by two Turkish nationals, Mr Kemal Demir and Ms Vicdan Baykara, the latter in her capacity as president of the trade union Tüm Bel Sen, (“the applicants”), on 8 October 1996.

facts.text: The applicants, Kemal Demir and Vicdan Baykara, were born in 1951 and 1958 and live in Gaziantep and Istanbul respectively. The first applicant was a member of the trade union Tüm Bel Sen and the second applicant was its president.

anchor.surface_text: 9.  The applicants, Kemal Demir and Vicdan Baykara, were born in 1951 and 1958 and live in Gaziantep and Istanbul respectively. The first applicant was a member of the trade union Tüm Bel Sen and the second applicant was its president.

facts.text: The trade union Tüm Bel Sen was founded in 1990 by civil servants from various localities under the Civil Servants Act (Law no. 657). Its objective was to promote democratic trade unionism to further the aspirations and claims of its members. Its head office is located in Istanbul.

anchor.surface_text: 10.  The trade union Tüm Bel Sen was founded in 1990 by civil servants from various localities under the Civil Servants Act (Law no. 657). Under Article 2 of its constitution its objective is to promote democratic trade unionism to further the aspirations and claims of its members. Its head office is located in Istanbul.

facts.text: On 27 February 1993 Tüm Bel Sen entered into a collective agreement with Gaziantep Municipal Council for a period of two years from 1 January 1993 concerning all aspects of working conditions including salaries, allowances and welfare services.

anchor.surface_text: 11.  On 27 February 1993 Tüm Bel Sen entered into a collective agreement with Gaziantep Municipal Council for a period of two years from 1 January 1993. The agreement concerned all aspects of the working conditions of Gaziantep Municipal Council’s employees, including salaries, allowances and welfare services.

facts.text: The Municipal Council defaulted on certain obligations under the agreement, particularly financial ones, leading the first applicant to bring civil proceedings against it in the Gaziantep District Court on 18 June 1993.

anchor.surface_text: 12.  As the Municipal Council had defaulted on certain of its obligations under the agreement, in particular those of a financial nature, the first applicant, as a representative of the union, brought civil proceedings against it in the Gaziantep District Court (the “District Court”) on 18 June 1993.

facts.text: On 22 June 1994 the District Court found in favour of Tüm Bel Sen. Gaziantep Municipal Council appealed on points of law.

anchor.surface_text: 13.  In a judgment of 22 June 1994 the District Court found in favour of Tüm Bel Sen. Gaziantep Municipal Council appealed on points of law.

facts.text: On 13 December 1994 the Court of Cassation quashed the District Court judgment, finding that although civil servants could form unions, they were not authorised to enter into collective agreements under the law at that time.

anchor.surface_text: 14.  On 13 December 1994 the Court of Cassation quashed the judgment of the court below. It found that, even though there was no legal bar preventing civil servants from forming unions, they were not, as the law stood, authorised to enter into collective agreements.

facts.text: On 28 March 1995 the District Court confirmed its earlier judgment, reasoning that the omission in domestic law to allow civil servants to enter collective agreements should be remedied in light of international treaties ratified by Turkey.

anchor.surface_text: 15.  In a judgment of 28 March 1995 the District Court confirmed its earlier judgment on the ground that, despite the fact that the domestic statute contained no express provision affording unions formed by civil servants the right to enter into collective agreements, this omission had to be remedied in the light of international treaties such as the relevant convention of the International Labour Organisation, which had already been ratified by Turkey.

facts.text: On 6 December 1995 the Court of Cassation quashed the District Court judgment again, ruling that at the time the union was formed, the law did not permit civil servants to form trade unions and that international labour conventions had not been incorporated into domestic law.

anchor.surface_text: 16.  On 6 December 1995 the Court of Cassation quashed the judgment of the court below. It ruled that, at the time the union was formed, the applicable law did not permit civil servants to form trade unions. The union Tüm Bel Sen could not rely on the international labour conventions that dealt with such matters as they had not yet been incorporated into domestic law and no implementing legislation had been enacted. The Court of Cassation concluded that the union did not have legal personality or the capacity to enter into a collective agreement.

facts.text: An application for rectification by union representatives was dismissed by the Court of Cassation on 10 April 1996.

anchor.surface_text: 17.  An application for rectification lodged by representatives of the union was dismissed by the Court of Cassation on 10 April 1996.

facts.text: Following an audit of Gaziantep Municipal Council’s accounts by the Audit Court, the State asked members of Tüm Bel Sen to reimburse additional income they had received as a result of the now-defunct collective agreement.

anchor.surface_text: 18.  Following an audit of Gaziantep Municipal Council’s accounts by the Audit Court, the State asked the members of the union Tüm Bel Sen to reimburse the additional income they had purportedly received as a result of the defunct collective agreement.

facts.text: The applicants complained under Article 11 taken with Article 14 that domestic courts denied them the right to form a trade union and to enter into collective agreements.

anchor.surface_text: 3.  The applicants complained, under Article 11 of the Convention taken in conjunction with Article 14, that the domestic courts had denied them the right to form a trade union and to enter into collective agreements.

facts.text: The applicants and Government filed further written observations after the Chamber declared the application partly admissible on 23 September 2004.

anchor.surface_text: 7.  The applicants and the Government each filed further written observations (Rule 59 § 1).

facts.text: The applicants were represented by Mr Ayhan Kızılöz, a lawyer practising in Istanbul; the Turkish Government were represented by their Agent.

anchor.surface_text: 2.  The applicants were represented by Mr Ayhan Kızılöz, a lawyer practising in Istanbul. The Turkish Government (“the Government”) were represented by their Agent.

facts.text: The trade union Tüm Bel Sen persuaded Gaziantep Municipal Council to engage in collective bargaining and reached an agreement determining reciprocal obligations and duties.

anchor.surface_text: 37.  In the first place, the trade union Tüm Bel Sen persuaded the employer, Gaziantep Municipal Council, to engage in collective bargaining over questions that it regarded as important for the interests of its members and to reach an agreement in order to determine their reciprocal obligations and duties.

facts.text: The collective agreement was implemented and governed employer-employee relations within Gaziantep Municipal Council for two years, except for certain disputed financial provisions.

anchor.surface_text: 39.  Moreover, the collective agreement was implemented. For a period of two years, with the exception of certain financial provisions that were in dispute between the parties, the collective agreement governed all employer-employee relations within Gaziantep Municipal Council.

facts.text: The annulment of the collective agreement between the authority and the trade union, applied for two years, constituted interference with the applicants’ freedom of association under Article 11.

anchor.surface_text: 40.  Accordingly, the Court cannot but observe that the collective agreement that the applicants had previously entered into with their employer, in the present case, represented for the trade union Tüm Bel Sen the principal, if not the only, means of promoting and safeguarding the interests of its members. It follows that the annulment of the collective agreement between the authority and the trade union entered into two years earlier, and applied since then, constituted interference with the applicants’ freedom of association within the meaning of Article 11 of the Convention.

facts.text: The applicants acted in good faith when entering into the collective agreement because Turkey had ratified ILO Convention No. 98 securing the right to bargain collectively and enter into collective agreements.

anchor.surface_text: 44.  The Court notes that, at the material time, the applicants acted in good faith when they chose, as a collective action for the purpose of protecting their interests within the meaning of Article 11, the option of entering into a collective agreement, because Turkey had already ratified the International Labour Organisation Convention No. 98, which secures for all workers the right to bargain collectively and to enter into collective agreements.

facts.text: The Court of Cassation considered that the Turkish legislature had not yet provided for implementation of Convention No. 98, so the union could not rely on it domestically.

anchor.surface_text: 45.  The Turkish Court of Cassation considered that it could not apply those provisions in the present case on the ground that the Turkish legislature had not yet, at the material time, provided for the implementation of Convention No. 98.

facts.text: The respondent State declared null and void retrospectively a collective agreement entered into nearly three years earlier and applied since then, which the Court found unfair and a violation of Article 11.

anchor.surface_text: 46.  The Court considers that, following that judgment of the Court of Cassation, the respondent State, in declaring null and void retrospectively a collective agreement entered into nearly three years earlier and applied since then, acted unfairly in breach of its obligation to secure enjoyment of the rights protected under Article 11 of the Convention.

facts.text: The applicants claimed pecuniary damage of EUR 551 and non-pecuniary damage of EUR 14,880 (Demir) and EUR 148,810 (Baykara on behalf of the union).

anchor.surface_text:
50.  The first applicant, Kemal Demir, claimed that he had sustained pecuniary damage in the sum of 551 euros (EUR), in particular on account of his loss of thirteen years’ additional pay following the annulment of the collective agreement. As to non-pecuniary damage, resulting from his disappointment at being deprived of the means to assert his rights, he claimed EUR 14,880.

The second applicant, Vicdan Baykara, on behalf of the trade union that she represented and of its members, claimed compensation for non-pecuniary damage in the sum of EUR 148,810.

facts.text: The Court awarded Mr Kemal Demir EUR 500 for all heads of damage combined and Ms Vicdan Baykara EUR 20,000 for non-pecuniary damage to be distributed to union members.

anchor.surface_text:
52.  As to the claim submitted by the applicant Kemal Demir in respect of pecuniary damage, the Court notes that no documentary evidence has been adduced in support of the claim. It considers, however, that the sum which the applicant was obliged to pay back to the State following the annulment of the relevant collective agreement must be returned to him. Making its assessment on an equitable basis, the Court awards the applicant Kemal Demir EUR 500 for all heads of damage combined.

53.  As to the claim submitted in respect of non-pecuniary damage by the applicant Vicdan Baykara on behalf of the trade union she represented, the Court observes that at the material time the trade union Tüm Bel Sen was the principal union of the employees of Gaziantep Municipal Council. Its dissolution and the annulment of its collective agreement with the Council must have caused deep feelings of frustration among its members, because they were thus deprived of their sole, or at least principal, means of defending their interests.

Making its assessment on an equitable basis, the Court awards the sum of EUR 20,000 in respect of non-pecuniary damage to the members of the trade union Tüm Bel Sen. This sum is to be paid to the applicant Vicdan Baykara, who represents the trade union and who will be responsible for making this sum available to its members.
